scenes.heading: Trigonometry in 3D
scenes.sub: Find the flat triangle hiding inside the shape
scenes.say: Boxes, roofs, ramps and pyramids are three-dimensional. But every angle inside them can be found with the same tools you already know, once you spot the right-angled triangle hiding inside.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A coat hanger across a shoebox and its shadow on the floor
scenes.science: A space diagonal and its projection on the base
scenes.breaks: Real shadows depend on the light. A maths projection always drops straight down.
scenes.say: Push a coat hanger diagonally across a shoebox, from a bottom corner to the opposite top corner. With a light right above, its shadow runs along the floor diagonal. The hanger, its shadow and a vertical edge make a right-angled triangle standing up inside the box.

scenes.heading: Find it, flatten it, solve it
steps: SOH CAH TOA for the angle
scenes.say: The method has three parts. Find the right-angled triangle. Redraw it flat, with the right angle marked. Use Pythagoras for any missing side, then soh cah toa for the angle.

scenes.heading: Angle between a diagonal and the base
scenes.say: Here is a box, eight by six by five centimetres. Now the space diagonal A G, and its shadow on the base, the dashed diagonal A C. First, Pythagoras on the base: A C is ten. Triangle A C G has a right angle at C, so tan theta is five over ten. Theta is about twenty-six point six degrees.
scenes.caption: AC = √(8² + 6²) = 10 cm. tan θ = 5/10, so θ ≈ 26.6°.

scenes.heading: Pyramids: use half the diagonal
scenes.say: Now a square pyramid with base ten metres and height twelve. For a sloping edge, the right-angled triangle is V O B. O B is half the base diagonal, five root two. Tan theta is twelve over five root two, so theta is about fifty-nine point five degrees.
scenes.caption: OB = 5√2 m. tan θ = 12 ÷ 5√2, so θ ≈ 59.5°.

scenes.heading: Pyramid edge or face?

right.title: Sloping face VAB
points: Triangle VOM, M = middle of AB

scenes.say: Don’t mix these up. For a sloping edge, go from the centre to a corner: that’s half the diagonal. For a sloping face, go from the centre to the middle of an edge: that’s half the side.

points: Find the triangle, draw it flat
Line and plane: use its shadow
South and east lines meet at 90°
scenes.say: Quick recap. Find the triangle and draw it flat. Use Pythagoras on the base first. The angle between a line and a plane uses the line’s shadow. And for pyramids, edges use half the diagonal and faces use half the side. Now try the practice questions!
